Core safety principles

  • Use current national requirements, guidelines and product labels.
  • Check identity, allergies, dose units, interactions and patient-specific factors.
  • Do not consume unidentified plants or mushrooms.
  • For suspected poisoning or severe symptoms, seek urgent professional help.
  • Do not use this provisional library as an emergency protocol.

Poison Safety & Toxicology

General public-facing first actions. Specialist treatment pathways, antidote selection and dosing require current clinical-toxicology references, local availability checks and qualified oversight.

Immediate actions / Tallaabooyinka degdegga ah

English
  1. Protect yourself from exposure.
  2. Call local emergency services or a poison centre if available.
  3. Do not induce vomiting.
  4. Do not give food, drink, home remedies, charcoal or antidotes unless instructed by a qualified professional.
  5. Keep packaging/label and note the time and route of exposure if safe.
Af-Soomaali
  1. Naftaada ka ilaali sunta.
  2. La xiriir gurmadka degdegga ah ama xarun sunta talo ka bixisa haddii la heli karo.
  3. Ha ku qasbin qofka inuu matago.
  4. Ha siin cunto, cabitaan, dawo-guri, dhuxul daawo ah ama sun-celin ilaa xirfadle kuu sheego.
  5. Haddii ay ammaan tahay, hay baakadka/summadda oo qor waqtiga iyo sida sunta u gashay.

Emergency red flags

Seek emergency care now for unconsciousness, seizure, breathing difficulty, collapse, severe confusion, severe burns, or suspected intentional ingestion. Do not delay transfer to search this application.

For skin or eye exposure, rinse with copious clean water while arranging professional advice unless product-specific emergency guidance says otherwise. For inhalation, move to fresh air only if it is safe for the rescuer.

Medicines & dosing errors

Stop further exposure where safe, obtain the exact product/concentration, route, amount and time, and seek urgent clinical/toxicology advice. Do not apply a universal antidote sequence to every exposure.

Plants & mushrooms

Never consume a wild plant or mushroom based on smell, one visual feature or an online guess. Identification must be reliable and expert-confirmed. If ingestion is suspected, seek urgent advice.

Snake & scorpion incidents

Move away from the animal, limit unnecessary movement, remove constricting jewellery/clothing where practical, and seek urgent medical care. Do not cut, suck, burn, or apply a tight tourniquet. Local protocols and species-specific care are essential.

Hidden toxicology registry — scope

This app includes a safety-navigation section, not a covert or complete poison database. A proper clinical registry should document agent, exposure route, expected toxidrome, time course, red flags, first aid, investigations, antidote evidence, contraindications, monitoring, referral thresholds, source/date, and reviewer approval. High-risk dosing and detailed procedures must be restricted to an appropriately governed clinician-facing module and validated before use.

This section is general education, not a substitute for emergency services, poison-centre advice, or clinical assessment.

Offline Knowledge Assistant

This is a local keyword-retrieval helper. It searches embedded source texts and notes; it is not a generative AI model and cannot independently diagnose, prescribe, verify evidence or replace professional judgment.

Do not enter patient names, phone numbers, IDs, photographs, or other identifiable health information into a shared copy of this file.

Evidence, Safety & Editorial Governance

Evidence transparency is part of the product. The catalogue does not imply clinical approval, complete content, or successful real-device validation.

Evidence status legend

E0 / PROVISIONAL Imported or planned material without independent claim-by-claim verification in this app.

REVIEW REQUIRED Needs source/date check, applicability review, translation review and sign-off.

APPROVED Reserved for content with recorded reviewer approval and versioned change control. This standalone file does not certify any imported clinical manuscript as approved.

Minimum review record

  • Unique document/chapter/poster ID and version.
  • Author, accountable clinical reviewer and language reviewer.
  • Evidence source, publication date, access date and update status.
  • Population, indication, contraindications, monitoring and local adaptation.
  • Change log, approval date, next review date and withdrawal pathway.

Priority correction workflow

The available V27 correction register identifies safety-sensitive topics including epinephrine concentration errors, U-500 insulin errors, concentrated potassium chloride, sepsis evidence framing, toxic mushroom ingestion, wild-plant identification, tumor lysis syndrome, antimicrobial-resistance treatment selection and radiation contamination. Their presence in a register does not mean every correction is fully resolved or approved. Verify the current authoritative source and record reviewer sign-off before publishing protocols.

Step-by-Step Installation & Release Guide

Darusihha International Hospitals — Academic Press · Release V30.2

Knowledge with Compassion — Aqoon iyo Naxariis

Stage A — Open the standalone offline HTML on Android

  1. Tap the standalone HTML download link provided in this conversation and choose Download.
  2. Open Android My Files → Downloads.
  3. Tap Darusihha_Atlas_All-in-One_Offline_Reference_V30.html and choose Chrome or another full browser if prompted.
  4. Test Overview, Books & Reports, search, chapter index, poster catalogue, safety and governance tabs.
  5. Try Airplane mode. If the file preview disables scripts, open the file from My Files in a compatible browser. Local-file behavior differs by browser.

Stage B — Publish the installable PWA

  1. Download and extract the Darusihha Atlas PWA Release ZIP on a computer.
  2. Create or open a repository on GitHub and upload the package contents (not just the ZIP).
  3. Enable GitHub Pages or another static HTTPS host and follow the included deployment workflow.
  4. Open the live HTTPS URL and verify that the manifest, icons, page navigation and service-worker registration load without errors.
  5. Test on Android Chrome. Use the browser menu and choose Install app or Add to Home screen when offered.
  6. Load the app once online, then test offline behavior. The service worker can cache only resources configured in the package.

Stage C — Package an Android APK

  1. Use the live HTTPS website URL with a reputable PWA packaging tool such as PWABuilder.
  2. Resolve validation warnings; confirm app name, application ID, version and icons.
  3. Generate the Android package and follow the tool's current instructions for signing.
  4. Keep signing keys private. Do not share passwords, API keys or keystores in public repositories or WhatsApp groups.
  5. Install and test the APK on a test device before distribution. Google Play distribution has additional requirements.

Stage D — Final testing and WhatsApp distribution

  1. Test on at least one real Android phone: startup, navigation, search, text readability, logo and home-screen icon.
  2. Test airplane-mode behavior after an initial successful online load.
  3. Check every medical section for review status, source traceability, emergency warnings and privacy. Do not publish patient-identifying data.
  4. Share the HTTPS website link for easiest updates. Share the HTML or APK as a document only after testing and when appropriate.
  5. Record release version, date, known limitations and contact details. Keep a backup of the tested release.
What is already prepared: the release package includes the main HTML, manifest, service worker, app icons, logo asset and deployment instructions. What is not yet done: publishing to a hosting account, installing on your physical phone, confirming real-device offline operation, or generating/signing an APK.

Clinical and catalogue limitations

The Atlas is a provisional reference, not a substitute for current local protocols, product labels, emergency services or qualified clinical judgement. The 30-volume, 1,000-chapter and 200-poster figures describe catalogue architecture/slots, not fully completed publications. Review content and exclude private patient data before public release.
